newsitem.title: USA: Wellpoint posts lower profits after recapitalization.
newsitem.headline: Wellpoint posts lower profits after recapitalization.

text.p: WellPoint Health Networks Inc. said Tuesday its profits declined by about 13 percent in the third quarter, primarily as a result of increased costs related to its recapitalization in May.

WellPoint, one of the nation's largest publicly traded managed care companies, said its net income for the three months ended Sept. 30 fell to $45.1 million, or 68 cents a share, from $51.8 million, or 78 cents a share.
The company said its earnings were reduced by $8.9 million, or 13 cents a share, due to higher interest expenses, lower investment income and other costs associated with its recapitalization.
The recapitalization was the result of the conversion of Blue Cross of California, its principal shareholder, into a for-profit company.
Wellpoint, which is based in Woodland Hills, Calif., said its third-quarter revenues increased to $1.13 billion from $771.9 million, primarily due to acquisitions.

The company said revenues were helped by its May acquisitions of the life and health benefits management division of Massachusetts Mutual Life Insurance Co. and the commercial operations of Blue Cross of California.

WellPoint said revenues from premiums increased 46 percent to $1.05 billion as membership in its medical plans jumped to about 4.4 million from about 2.8 million at the end of last year's third quarter.

The company, whose products are marketed in California under the Blue Cross name and in other parts of the country under its UNICARE name, said its net income for the first nine months slipped to $155 million, or $2.33 a share, from $166.7 million, or $2.51 a share.
Revenues rose to $3.0 billion from $2.33 billion.
WellPoint's stock gave up 12.5 cents to $31.75 in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
